regime_context: Hong Kong thematic leadership is extremely narrow: only 4 of 17 themes are trend-eligible (Banks, Energy, High-Dividend Blue Chips, Conglomerates & Exchange), led by Banks. No theme has a proxy ETF flagged as scorable except China Tech & Internet and China Platform Megacaps (both rank bottom-quartile), so nearly all leans here are on unscorable names and conviction must stay low. Rotation is non-directional (absorption 0.46, one_narrative false), and the only validated leg is the absolute-trend gate for drawdown control.
emerging_watch: Watching whether China Tech & Internet (3033.HK, rank 13, mean-revert tag, currently ineligible) begins to narrow its score gap versus the leader and re-enter trend eligibility — the observable that retires this watch is its trend-gate eligibility flipping to true while the leader Banks remains above the 0.67 durability bar.

theses.subject: Energy (H-shares)
theses.thesis: Energy is the highest-ranked trend-eligible theme with the strongest durability_bar (0.76) and the broadest participation (breadth 0.8), and is marked hurst_tag='trend'. That combination says leadership is broad, sticky, and trend-healthy relative to the narrow, mixed-tag Banks at the top. Supported by trend-gate eligibility, durability, breadth, and trend tag rather than momentum rank.
evidence: eligible: true with rank 2 and score 0.983
breadth 0.8 — best breadth in the eligible set
theses.dissent: Energy leadership is one rank below Banks and cannot be graded against a proxy ETF here; the momentum attention is still on Financials, and a commodity-led H-share theme can unwind fast on global macro risk-off even if internal trend stats look clean.

falsifier.text: Energy (H-shares) breadth drops below 0.5 or its durability_bar falls below the Banks' before the 30-day check

check.reason: theme has no scalar etf_proxy → not cleanly scorable

theses.subject: Banks (H + HK)
theses.thesis: Banks is the dominant narrative leader with the highest momentum score and positive breadth (0.692), still trend-eligible. Despite the mixed hurst tag, leadership concentration plus adequate breadth supports staying with the trend rather than fading it. Supported by rank, eligible gate, and positive breadth; crowding is low so no size-down caution applies.
evidence: crowded: false, crowding_z 0.93 — no extension caution
theses.dissent: The hurst_tag is 'mixed' not 'trend', and the momentum rank itself has no forward return edge; Banks leadership is the most consensus and most headline-driven, making it vulnerable to a policy-surprise unwind in a high-unscheduled-news backdrop (unscheduled_share 0.75).

falsifier.text: Banks loses trend eligibility (falls out of the absolute-trend gate) while Energy holds eligibility

check.reason: theme has no scalar etf_proxy → not cleanly scorable

theses.subject: High-Dividend Blue Chips
theses.thesis: High-Dividend Blue Chips is trend-eligible with a reasonable durability_bar (0.65) and breadth above half (0.625). In a market with only four eligible themes, income-style defensives remaining trend-eligible argues for continuing to respect the trend, especially since crowding is absent and the validated edge is drawdown control via staying with eligible, durable names.
theses.dissent: This theme is unscorable and has a 'mixed' hurst tag; defensives can stay eligible purely by low volatility rather than genuine relative strength, and in a risk-on HK tape dividend names usually lag the cyclical leaders.

falsifier.text: High-Dividend Blue Chips breadth drops below 0.5 while both Banks and Energy remain eligible

check.reason: theme has no scalar etf_proxy → not cleanly scorable

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
